title: Reverse a Linked List
statement:
You are given `head`, the first node of a **singly linked list** (each node has a `val` and a `next` pointing to the following node; the last node's `next` is empty). An empty list is passed as an empty `head`.

Reverse the list and return the **new head**. (In the examples the list is shown as the list of its values.)

examples.explanation: The order of the nodes is reversed.

hints.nudge: Each node's 'next' pointer has to point backwards instead of forwards. What do you need to remember so you do not lose the rest of the list?
hints.pattern: Walk the list with three pointers: previous, current, next.
hints.pseudocode:
prev = null; cur = head
while cur:
  nxt = cur.next
  cur.next = prev
  prev = cur; cur = nxt
return prev
hints.walkthrough: Copying the values into an array and rebuilding works but uses O(n) extra space. Instead reverse the links in place: before changing cur.next, save the next node, then point cur.next at the previous node and move both pointers forward. When cur becomes empty, prev is the old last node, which is the new head. O(n) time, O(1) space.
